official.deadline_note: No separate Karsh deadline; consideration follows Duke's admission cycle. Early Decision: application 2 November 2026, financial aid applications (CSS Profile and FAFSA) 3 November 2026, additional aid documents 15 November 2026. Regular Decision: application 4 January 2027, financial aid applications 1 February 2027, midyear grade report 15 February 2027. Transfer deadline 15 March, but Duke publishes that need-based financial aid is not available to international transfer students.
official.application_cycle: 2026-27 admission cycle (first-year applicants entering as Duke's Class of 2031)
official.status_note: Duke's admissions site states the posted requirements and deadlines represent the 2026-27 admission cycle; the Common Application is available and both Early Decision (2 November) and Regular Decision (4 January) deadlines are still ahead, with decisions released mid-December (Early Decision) and late March/early April (Regular Decision).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Official FAQ wording: 'What does it cover? Your tuition, room and board, mandatory fees, demonstrated need that exceeds those costs, and three summers of funding for research, unpaid internships, and other opportunities that will advance your academic career.'

official.application_route: Submit the Common Application (or QuestBridge Application) to Duke with the financial aid interest box marked 'yes', then file the CSS Profile by the aid deadline; Karsh consideration is automatic.
official.citizenship_residency: Must be a citizen of a country outside the United States; dual U.S./other-country citizens are not eligible
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is restricted to international (non-U.S.-citizen) applicants
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: No field restriction is published; applicants choose between Trinity College of Arts & Sciences and the Pratt School of Engineering and may be considered under either
official.duration: Full four-year undergraduate degree; Duke publishes that it issues four-year aid awards for international applicants, automatically renewed for subsequent years at Duke
official.description: Founded in 2010 thanks to a generous donation from Martha L. and Bruce A. Karsh, the Karsh International Scholarship brings together a cohort of international undergraduates at Duke who promote interdisciplinary inquiry, academic research, and scholarship in the service of society. International applicants must have demonstrated financial need to be eligible, and there is no separate application: candidates apply to Duke University and request financial aid.
official.program_type: Need-based international undergraduate scholarship administered by Duke University's Office of University Scholars and Fellows
official.english_requirement: Not required. Duke recommends, but does not require, an English proficiency test for non-native English speakers or applicants not studying in an English-medium curriculum; minimum scores expected: IELTS 7, TOEFL iBT 100 (TOEFL paper-delivered 75), Duolingo 130, PTE Academic 70, Cambridge C1 Advanced or C2 Proficiency 180. Self-reported scores are accepted and the Duolingo submission is free.

applicant_utility.summary: The Karsh Scholarship is not a separate competition: it is awarded through Duke's need-based aid process to admitted international first-years, so your admission and funding answer arrive together. The single highest-risk field on your application is the financial aid interest box - mark it 'yes' when you first submit, because Duke states that international applicants admitted with 'no financial aid interest' become ineligible to apply for aid at any point. Treat the financial aid deadlines, not the admission deadline, as the real cut-off: CSS Profile by 3 November (Early Decision) or 1 February (Regular Decision).
applicant_utility.best_fit: Outstanding international first-year applicants who can document substantial financial need and for whom Duke is a genuine first choice (Early Decision is binding).
application_readiness_checklist: Mark the financial aid interest box 'yes' on the Duke/Common Application before submitting, and email Undergraduate Admissions immediately if it was missed
Open the CSS Profile as soon as it goes live on 1 October and file it well before 3 November (ED) or 1 February (RD)
Brief your school counselor early: the transcript, Secondary School Report and counselor recommendation must come directly from the school
Line up two teacher recommendations from core academic subjects (one from math or science if applying to Pratt)
Draft the two required 250-word Duke essays (Why Duke; Communities) with specifics that only fit Duke
Assemble translated financial documents in advance: foreign tax records plus employer income statements in English with the original documents and USD exchange rates noted
Request the $85 application fee waiver through the Common Application if cost is a barrier
Decide deliberately whether to submit English test scores - Duke recommends but does not require them, and self-reported Duolingo or IELTS scores are accepted
common_rejection_risks: Holding dual U.S./other-country citizenship, which makes you ineligible regardless of need or academics
Already holding a B.A. or B.S. degree, which the official FAQ rules out
Failing to tick the financial aid interest box on the original application - a mistake Duke says cannot be fixed later
Applying as a transfer student: Duke publishes that need-based aid is not available to international transfer students
Waiting for a nomination or assuming a separate scholarship form exists - none does, so nothing extra gets submitted
Filing the CSS Profile late or ignoring an IDOC document request, which delays the aid offer even though total eligibility does not change
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Duke's published 2026-27 cost of attendance is $103,180-$103,975 before aid (tuition $73,740, fees, housing and food billed at about $98,788-$98,848, plus books, personal expenses and only a domestic transportation estimate). The award covers demonstrated need above billed costs, but international airfare home, U.S. visa and SEVIS fees, and any expense above the calculated need are not inside the published budget.
document_audit: Transcripts and School Report forms must arrive from the school directly - documents sent by the applicant are not accepted
Translated transcripts must be accompanied by the original documents
IDOC financial documents need the English statement from both parents' employers stating annual income, with currency converted to U.S. dollars
Parents who do not file taxes or are self-employed must complete a non-filer form; plan for this before the request arrives
Midyear grade reports are due 15 February, so keep your counselor engaged after you submit
alerts: Early Decision is binding - only choose it if Duke is truly your first choice, since the aid offer and the admission decision come together in mid-December
The aid deadlines sit after the application deadlines (3 November vs 2 November; 1 February vs 4 January), so a submitted application does not mean a complete aid file
International aid applicants are read in a more selective pool - Duke states the admit rate for foreign citizens seeking aid is usually less than half the overall rate
Aid awards for international students are issued for four years and renew automatically, but you must attend a financial aid session on arrival at Duke for the aid to be applied
Duke is test-optional for 2026-27, so skipping the SAT/ACT does not disadvantage you, but English scores remain useful evidence for non-native speakers
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Common Application plus CSS Profile filed online by the deadline; Duke emails an Application Checklist, requests any IDOC financial documents, then releases admission and the aid offer together in mid-December (ED) or late March/early April (RD).
